clue.text: An easy putt chap apparently missed in a crisis?

parts.note: an gives the single letter A
a tap-in is a putt so short it can hardly be missed in golf

indicators.note: the clue hints that the chap has 'ap' missing, as if the opening of apparently had been dropped from him

parts.note: chap as written, before its letters are trimmed

explanation.surface: A golfer misses a putt anyone could sink, in a moment of crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparently missed' strips AP from CHAP, leaving CH.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for 'if need be, in an emergency' is at a pinch, the British form of in a pinch.

clue.text: Hot current in river? On the contrary

indicators.note: in signals one piece placed inside another
says the containment runs the other way: the river goes inside the current, not the reverse

parts.note: topical means current, of present interest

explanation.surface: A warm current flowing in a river, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Tropical weather is hot, so the word serves as a synonym for sweltering.

clue.text: Turkish official remains in power — Ankara's foremost

indicators.note: in puts the remains inside the letters around them

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics

indicators.note: foremost picks the front letter of Ankara

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A Turkish official keeps hold of power, with Ankara in the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A title for a high-ranking officer or governor in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Study of plants and animals that could make authority snarl

indicators.note: says the letters of the following words could be rearranged to form something new

explanation.surface: A field of study whose name could be twisted to make officials growl.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional name for the scientific observation of living things and their habitats.

clue.text: Hectare observed to contain black dinosaur?

parts.note: HA is the abbreviation for hectare

indicators.note: to contain signals the outer letters wrapping round another piece

parts.note: observed means seen
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone measures land and spots a dark dinosaur within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative dinosaur is a person past their prime and out of date, which is what a has-been is.

clue.text: Chap's error, with loss of station

indicators.note: says the station's letters are removed from the error

parts.note: an error is a mistake

explanation.surface: A man's blunder costs him his post.
explanation.definitionFit: A common male first name, so a chap might be called this.

clue.text: Nut, excellent, turning up under pavement

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places one piece below the other

parts.note: macadam is road surfacing, a kind of pavement

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written here as AI

explanation.surface: A fine nut is found turning up beneath the paving.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich round nut from an Australian tree, often sold as a snack.

clue.text: Fool around, keeping lieutenant (English) dressed for the Black Watch?

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the other letters go within

parts.note: to kid around is to fool around

explanation.surface: A joker larks about with an English lieutenant in a Scottish regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: The Black Watch is a famous Scottish Highland regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Highland regiments wear the traditional Scottish kilt, so their soldiers are dressed that way.

clue.text: Tolerate nausea with ices dished up in light yellow liquid

parts.note: to bear is to tolerate

indicators.note: dished up suggests food prepared afresh, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Put up with queasiness while ices are served in a pale sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale yellow sauce of egg yolk, butter and tarragon, served with steak.

clue.text: Party and group retaining King's part of England

indicators.note: retaining means holding within, so the king goes inside

parts.note: a do is a party
a set is a group
R is the abbreviation for king, from the Latin rex

explanation.surface: A party and a set of people keep hold of a royal's region.
explanation.definitionFit: A county on the south coast of England, so a part of the country.

clue.text: Number encountered in science lesson, initially in outline

indicators.note: the number is met inside the science, so its letters are placed within

parts.note: ten is a number

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of lesson

explanation.surface: A figure crops up in a science class, drawn first as an outline.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-out template used to paint a shape, so it gives an outline.

clue.text: Dissent to lose vigour in dreadful conclusion to conference

indicators.note: in places the sagging inside the dreadful

parts.note: dire means dreadful
to sag is to droop and lose vigour

indicators.note: conclusion to takes the last letter of conference

explanation.surface: Dissenters wilt at the miserable close of a conference.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissent is to differ in opinion, a synonym for this verb.

clue.text: Showing more colour, shifting one steering device

indicators.note: shifting means removing, so the one is moved out

parts.note: ruddier means redder, showing more colour
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone blushing deeper while shifting one steering device.
explanation.definitionFit: The hinged blade at the stern of a boat that steers it.

clue.text: Redirected magma leak? No, run! Grab everything you can!

indicators.note: redirected means sent a different way, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Lava escapes in a new direction; a voice yells to flee and seize what you can.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means stretching to take as much as possible for yourself.

clue.text: Quick buck? Many eyes excitedly gathering round

indicators.note: gathering means taking in, so the round letter goes inside
excitedly means in an agitated way, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: the words as written are the anagram fodder
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Many watchers gather eagerly round a fast deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick buck is cash earned with little effort, the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Plot of substantial size providing lots of wood

parts.note: a plan is a plot or scheme
king as in king-size, meaning large

explanation.surface: A large plot of land supplies plenty of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Planking is boards collectively, a quantity of sawn wood.

clue.text: Rising and falling aboard ship, Henry and friend appear uncertain

indicators.note: aboard puts something within the ship's letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
hilly land rises and falls
H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Pitching about on a ship, Henry and a pal look unsure.
explanation.definitionFit: To dither and hesitate, appearing unable to make up one's mind.

clue.text: Oxford college lecturer in the area?

parts.note: an acre is a unit of area

explanation.surface: Asking whether a lecturer is somewhere nearby in Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: A graduate college of Oxford University, named after a Tudor physician.

clue.text: Judge's point of view leading to contention

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for judge
an angle is a point of view

explanation.surface: A judge's perspective sparks an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A jangle is an old word for a noisy quarrel or wrangle, hence dispute.

clue.text: Animal, second available in market

indicators.note: in places the second inside the market

parts.note: a mart is a market
a mo is a moment or second

explanation.surface: A creature for sale briefly at the market.
explanation.definitionFit: A marmot is an example: a burrowing rodent of mountain regions.

clue.text: Part of aircraft one cracked? Bring in most of a further one

indicators.note: bring in places the trimmed piece inside the cracked one
cracked means broken, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word as written is the anagram fodder

indicators.note: most of drops the last letter

parts.note: a second is a further one

explanation.surface: An aircraft part has cracked, so fit nearly another one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked' rearranges the word one into NOE, and the trimmed further one sits between its second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The cone-shaped front tip of an aircraft or rocket.

clue.text: Better run to island — this one?

parts.note: to cap is to better or outdo
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Is it better to dash to this island?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'island' before it: the answer is an island itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian island in the Bay of Naples, the island the clue points to.

clue.text: Fellow chasing information of no specific type

indicators.note: chasing means following, so the fellow comes after

parts.note: gen is informal British for information
Eric is a man's name, a fellow

explanation.surface: A man pursues facts that turn out vague.
explanation.definitionFit: Generic means general, not particular to any one kind.

clue.text: University degree securing job as secretary — presumably not this!

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the job goes inside

parts.note: a PA is a personal assistant, a secretarial job

explanation.surface: A graduate lands a secretarial post, hopefully with a salary.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone landing a job hopes it is not without wages.

clue.text: Bank definitely missing a pound

indicators.note: missing means the named letters are taken away

parts.note: really means definitely
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: A bank is surely short of a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank on something is to count on it, the same as depend.

clue.text: Still batting? Great scores for openers when night watchmen appear

parts.note: even means still, as in even more
in cricket, a batsman who is batting is in

indicators.note: for openers takes the first letters of the words

explanation.surface: Still at the crease, great runs flow until the night watchmen come in.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a night watchman is a lower-order batsman sent in late in the day; here it is literal guards on night shift.
explanation.definitionFit: Night guards come on duty as darkness falls, in the late part of the day.
